nodes.text: Let $A$ be the set of $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that there exist $1\leq m_1<\cdots <m_k=n$ with $\sum\tfrac{1}{m_i}=1$. Explore $A$. In particular, does $A$ have density $1$?

#292 : [ErGr80,p.35] number theory | unit fractions Straus observed that $A$ is closed under multiplication. Furthermore, it is easy to see that $A$ does not contain any prime power. The answer is yes, as proved by Martin [Ma00] , who in fact proved that if $B=\mathbb{N}\backslash A$ then, for all large $x$,\[\frac{\lvert B\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x}\asymp \frac{\log\log x}{\log x},\]and also gave an essentially complete description of $B$ as those integers which are small multiples of prime powers. van Doorn has observed that if $n\in A$ (with $n>1$) then $2n\in A$ also, since if $\sum \frac{1}{m_i}=1$ then $\frac{1}{2}+\sum\frac{1}{2m_i}=1$ also.
